skill.name: pubmed-database
skill.description: Direct REST API guide for PubMed searches, E-utilities workflows, MeSH query building, batch retrieval, and citation management.
skill.summary: Build PubMed queries and use NCBI E-utilities for repeatable biomedical literature retrieval.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives in context: placeholder API keys, expected NCBI links, PubMed API examples, and Markdown query examples. No embedded secrets, executable shell commands, prompt injection, or covert exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: API key examples use query parameters and placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Add a note that real API keys should be stored outside shared files, redacted from logs, and rotated if exposed.

remediation.issue: HTTP examples omit defensive request handling.
remediation.suggestion: Show timeouts, explicit User-Agent headers, response checks, retry backoff, and rate-limit handling in code examples.

remediation.issue: Markdown query examples can be mistaken for shell backtick execution by simple scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label fenced examples as text or PubMed query syntax to reduce static-analysis noise.

static_findings.snippet: Include the API key in requests using the `&api_key` parameter:
- Free full text: Add `AND free full text[sb]` to query
- Has abstract: Add `AND hasabstract[text]` to query
Grep pattern for query examples: `diabetes|cancer|cardiovascular|clinical trial|systematic review`
- Respect rate limits to avoid service disruption
- Export early and often to avoid losing search results

content.value_statement: Biomedical literature searches can miss key studies or produce unmanageable result sets. This skill helps build PubMed queries and use E-utilities for repeatable retrieval.
actual_capabilities: Guides Boolean, MeSH, field tag, date, and article type query construction.
Documents ESearch, EFetch, ESummary, EPost, ELink, EInfo, EGQuery, ESpell, and ECitMatch usage.
Shows Python requests examples for PubMed search and abstract retrieval.
Explains rate limits, API key use, history server workflows, and batch retrieval.
Provides workflows for systematic reviews, citation discovery, export, and literature monitoring.
limitations: It does not replace PubMed, NCBI Entrez, or Biopython; users must execute requests themselves.
API examples use placeholders and need a valid NCBI API key for higher rate limits.
PubMed does not always provide full text; publisher or institution access may be required.
Large searches need batching, caching, and rate limiting to avoid errors.

use_cases.title: Build a Literature Search
use_cases.description: Create a PubMed query with MeSH terms, synonyms, field tags, date limits, and article type filters.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Systematic Review
use_cases.description: Translate a PICO question into a reproducible search strategy and document filters for screening.

use_cases.title: Automate Citation Retrieval
use_cases.description: Plan E-utilities calls for PMIDs, abstracts, summaries, related articles, and batch export.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build a PubMed query for [topic]. Include MeSH terms, title and abstract terms, date limits, and article type filters.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Search Precision
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PubMed query: [query]. Suggest changes that improve precision without removing important synonyms.

prompt_templates.title: Plan API Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an E-utilities workflow for [research question]. Include search, fetch, batching, rate limits, caching, and output format choices.

prompt_templates.title: Design Review Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this PICO question into a documented PubMed strategy: [question]. Include MeSH terms, synonyms, filters, search history steps, and export guidance.

output_examples.input: Search for recent randomized controlled trials on type 2 diabetes and metformin.
output_examples.output: Suggested search: diabetes mellitus, type 2 with MeSH terms, metformin in title or abstract, randomized controlled trial publication type, and a recent date range.
Use ESearch with history enabled, then retrieve records in batches with EFetch. Add caching, backoff, and rate-limit handling.

output_examples.input: Find related articles for a known PMID.
output_examples.output: Use PubMed similar articles or ELink neighbor results, then inspect MeSH terms and citation links for discovery.

best_practices: Document the full search string, filters, database, and search date for reproducibility.
Combine MeSH terms with synonyms and title or abstract terms to improve coverage.
Respect NCBI rate limits and include a clear User-Agent for API requests.
anti_patterns: Putting a real API key directly into shared prompts, notebooks, or documentation.
Relying on one keyword without synonyms, MeSH terms, or field tags.
Bulk-fetching large result sets without batching, caching, or backoff.

faq.question: Does this skill search PubMed directly?
faq.answer: It provides instructions and API patterns. Actual requests require your tool or script with internet access.

faq.question: Do I need an NCBI API key?
faq.answer: No for basic use. A key raises rate limits, but real keys should not be hard-coded in shared files.

faq.question: Can it retrieve full text articles?
faq.answer: PubMed primarily provides citations and abstracts. Full text depends on PubMed Central, publishers, or institutional access.

faq.question: Can I use it for systematic reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports PICO planning, MeSH terms, Boolean logic, search documentation, and export workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace Biopython?
faq.answer: No. Bio.Entrez may be simpler for Python workflows. This skill focuses on direct REST API usage.

faq.question: What data formats are covered?
faq.answer: It covers PubMed XML, JSON summaries, MEDLINE text, abstract text, and citation exports.
